sample_unit: stroke patients (72 baseline, 102 after AI deployment); diagnostic accuracy on 864 NCCT scans
models_evaluated: AI-based automated NCCT head interpretation software (qER-type device, name not stated in text)

links.outcome: Time to intervention from NCCT imaging before vs after AI deployment in stroke patients
links.effect: Median TTI fell from 80 min (IQR 56.8-139.5) at baseline to 58.5 min (IQR 30.3-118.2) after AI deployment (location shift -21.0, 95% CI -38.0 to -7.0).
links.quote: Impact analysis in a total of 174 stroke patients (72 in baseline and 102 after deployment) demonstrated a significant reduction of median TTI from 80 minutes (IQR: 56·8-139·5) during baseline to 58·50 (IQR: 30·3-118.2) minutes after AI deployment (Wilcoxon rank sum test-location shift: -21·0, 95% CI: -38·0, -7·0).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the clinical impact (time to intervention) of deploying an AI diagnostic tool for non-contrast CT brain scans in a rural hospital, comparing pre- versus post-deployment periods.
